key_highlights: Unemployment hits 5-year high of 4.6% in August, yet RBA signals further rate hikes, testing credibility of its inflation mandate
ASX slumped on bond-market volatility rattling Wall Street; miners rose while oil stocks struggled, index closed flat
AUD weakened sharply against USD on US economic outperformance; 'Trump effect' widening cracks in global markets
Diesel export ban fears from US could push Australian diesel past $4/L with rationing risk
Rare earths and gold exploration activity accelerating: Lindian, Critica/Jupiter, Forrestania, Critical Resources, Aurum all advancing projects
Intergenerational Report 2026 flags urgent tax reform need; property prices falling on rising listings and weak demand
Medicare AI hack exposes cybersecurity vulnerabilities in health sector; $16B Aussie tech firm faces China-link scrutiny

sectors.trend: Miners outperformed on the day (48); rare earths pipeline expanding with Lindian stacking ore (13), Critica securing Jupiter offtake (51), Forrestania lifting British Hill gold past 210k oz (17), Critical Resources surging on Suriname gold (52), Aurum raising $52.5M for West African gold (53). Coal sector under pressure as mine owners abandon rehabilitation (8).
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX benefit from broad commodity resilience. Small-cap rare earths (LRE.AX, CRG.AX) and gold juniors (FRT.AX, CRU.AX) see elevated speculative interest. Coal names (BRL.AX, WDS.AX) face ESG and policy headwinds.

sectors.trend: RBA committed to further hikes despite 4.6% unemployment (5, 39), supporting net interest margins but raising credit-loss concerns. Bond-market volatility (11, 25) pressures equity valuations. Intergenerational Report (26) signals future tax reform risk.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from higher rates short-term but face NPL risk as unemployment rises. Bond yields rising pressures REITs and growth equities.

sectors.trend: Diesel price fears from potential US export ban (23, 36, 45) create supply-risk premium. Nuclear energy debate intensifies (41). Energy policy credibility questioned (56, 58). Oil stocks struggled on the day (48).
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, AWE.AX, SXG.AX face input-cost and policy uncertainty. LNG names (WDS.AX, GWO.AX) relatively insulated. Energy transition stocks gain narrative support from nuclear debate.

sectors.trend: Over half of renters financially struggling (18); property prices falling on rising listings and weak demand (54). Jetstar industrial action (74) and Sydney Airport strikes (7) disrupt consumer travel. Qantas Sydney-NY non-stop announced (57).
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX, SPG.AX) pressured by falling property values and rising rates. WES.AX, WOW.AX face consumer squeeze. QAN.AX benefits from route expansion; JPA.AX faces operational disruption.

sectors.trend: Medicare AI hack (14, 28) exposes health-sector cybersecurity gaps. $16B Aussie tech firm in China-link dispute (47). AI agent adoption accelerating globally (63, 73).
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX face regulatory and cybersecurity scrutiny. Tech names exposed to China decoupling risk. AI infrastructure beneficiaries (global) see momentum.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim consumer discretionary and travel names

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain range-bound to slightly lower over 1–3 months. RBA hike and 4.6% unemployment create stagflation overhang. Bond-market volatility (11, 25) caps equity multiples. Miners and banks provide relative strength; REITs, energy, and consumer lag. AUD weakness is a partial offset for exporters.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautious. Intergenerational Report (26) may trigger tax reform debate, adding policy uncertainty. Property correction continues. Energy transition and nuclear debate (41) could reshape capex cycles. Rare earths and critical minerals remain structural growth themes. Global 'Trump effect' (20) and US outperformance (37) keep AUD pressured, supporting commodity exporters.
